authority: SEED, NOT AUTHORITY. rust-toolchain.toml at the workspace root is the only pin cargo reads for a workspace build, because rustup resolves from the current directory and every Makefile target builds from the root. This file is read by ToolchainLifecycle (crates/cynic-host/src/toolchain/port.rs), which observes the live rustc, reconciles, and may run `rustup override set`. It is never compared against that observation, so it can disagree with the build without anything noticing — which is how it did.

measured.method: cargo check -v prints the rustc binary it invokes; the toolchain directory name identifies the channel
measured.note: The six crates/*/rust-toolchain.toml files are read only when the working directory is inside that crate. No Makefile target does that. They are left in place as documentation of an intended per-crate toolchain; they are inert for the build.
